principle_text: When the persuadee expresses reluctance or a desire to keep their resources, avoid making direct donation requests that may cause immediate resistance or refusal.
When the persuadee declines a donation but shows emotional conflict, you should acknowledge their decision empathetically to build rapport and create openness for further persuasion.
When the persuadee expresses reluctance to donate and skepticism about the charity, avoid focusing on personal financial needs that reinforce their hesitation.
When the persuadee expresses skepticism or discomfort, you should use humor and candidness to create a relaxed atmosphere that encourages curiosity and engagement.
When the persuadee expresses competing moral responsibilities, avoid emphasizing moral obligations that may increase their sense of pressure or guilt.

When the persuadee expresses skepticism or humor about donation requests without commitment, avoid providing neutral or purely factual statements that do not encourage positive engagement or donation intent.
When the persuadee expresses serious personal financial hardship, avoid minimizing or dismissing their struggles as it can alienate them and reduce their willingness to engage.
When the persuadee expresses financial hardship and hesitation, avoid shifting focus to your own donations without addressing their concerns or providing clear information about the cause.
When the persuadee expresses personal hardship or emotional distress, avoid pressing them to donate immediately or insisting on specific donation actions.

When the persuadee shows empathy but no increased willingness to donate, avoid making statements that only acknowledge the situation without connecting it to a specific call to action or donation opportunity.
When the persuadee responds with openness to transition from casual to serious topics, you should use lighthearted and respectful language to smoothly introduce the donation conversation.
When the persuadee shows openness to discuss serious topics, you should clarify the donation context and ask open-ended questions about the charity to encourage engagement and information sharing.
